title: SSO with Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC): registration is refused (userinfo on graph.microsoft.com), the groups claim never reaches the group mapping (userinfo replaces the id_token), and mailbox-less users fail with missing_user_info
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, cloud `main` built image (framework pin `e24136c2`, `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12), licensed. Live Microsoft Entra ID test tenant: app registration with `groupMembershipClaims: SecurityGroup` and optional id-token claims `email`, `upn`, `given_name`, `family_name`. Browser walk-through for objectstack-ai/cloud#3666.

## 1. Registration is refused
Setup → SSO Providers → Register SSO Provider, issuer `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`. The toast reads:

> Untrusted OIDC discovery URL: The userinfo_endpoint "https://graph.microsoft.com/oidc/userinfo" is not trusted by your trusted origins configuration.

`AuthManager.ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` auto-trusts only the origins written in the request body (issuer and explicit `oidcConfig` endpoints). Entra's discovery document puts `userinfo_endpoint` on a different host, so it is refused, and the form has no field to name it. The workaround used for the rest of this run was `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://graph.microsoft.com`, which also widens the CSRF allow-list. Okta did not hit this because all its endpoints share the issuer host.

**Expected:** trust the public-routable origins of the endpoints in the fetched discovery document of the issuer being registered, or at least a known IdP list. Today every Entra customer hits this on day one.

## 2. Group → permission-set mapping never applies for Entra OIDC
- With the mapping `providerId: entra-oidc`, `groupExternalId: <group object id>`, a JIT sign-in of a group member creates the account but grants **nothing**.
- Cause: when a provider has a `userInfoEndpoint`, `@better-auth/sso` builds `userInfo` (and `mapping.extraFields`, where the groups claim is read) **only from the userinfo response** and ignores the verified id_token. Entra's userinfo returns `sub`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `picture`, `email` — no `groups`.
- **Confirmed** by removing `userInfoEndpoint` from the stored `oidc_config` (diagnostic only): the next member signed in → granted; a re-login of an existing member → granted; after removing the member from the group in Entra and re-login → grant removed. So the projection itself works; the claim never reaches it.

**Expected:** read `extraFields` (and the standard claims as fallback) from the verified id_token when userinfo does not carry them, or let the provider opt out of userinfo. Also note that Entra replaces `groups` with an overage pointer (`_claim_names`) above ~200 groups, which needs handling or documenting.

## 3. Users without a mailbox cannot sign in
Entra omits `email` from the id_token and userinfo when the user has no `mail` attribute, which is common for cloud-only or unlicensed users. Sign-in ends with `error=invalid_provider&error_description=missing_user_info`, which the login page shows as "the sign-in link expired" (#32087). Setting `mail` on the users fixed it.

**Expected:** a documented "Map: Email claim" value for Entra (`preferred_username` / `upn`), the form suggesting it for `login.microsoftonline.com` issuers, and a refusal that names the missing claim.

## What works with Entra OIDC (once registered)
- SP-initiated sign-in, including MFA at Entra.
- JIT off → `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`.
- JIT on → account created as IdP-Provisioned with the right name.
- Sign-out ends the local session, but Entra's session lets the next SSO in without a password (#32087).
